entities.name: Primary pulmonary lymphoepithelial carcinoma
entities.anchor: Pulmonary lymphoepithelial carcinoma → EBV-driven, nonsmoker-predominant, classic NSCLC drivers usually absent.
snv: Notable absence — canonical NSCLC drivers (EGFR, KRAS, BRAF) are rarely mutated
cnv: Associated — EBV-associated copy-number alterations and NF-κB pathway dysregulation
other: Viral driver — Epstein–Barr virus (EBV; EBER-positive in >90% of Asian cohorts, lower in Western cohorts); high PD-L1 expression
entities.pitfall: Reclassified under squamous cell carcinoma in WHO Thoracic 5th ed. Morphologically and immunophenotypically identical to metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma; nasopharyngeal imaging/endoscopy is mandatory before diagnosing a lung primary.

entities.name: Fetal adenocarcinoma of the lung
entities.anchor: Low-grade fetal lung adenocarcinoma → CTNNB1 exon 3; high-grade → TP53.
snv: Driver (low-grade) — CTNNB1 exon 3 activating variants driving nuclear/cytoplasmic β-catenin accumulation
Driver (high-grade) — TP53 inactivation; EGFR and KRAS variants are uncommon
cnv: Associated — higher chromosomal instability in high-grade than in pure low-grade tumors
entities.pitfall: Frequently expresses neuroendocrine markers (synaptophysin, chromogranin) and TTF-1, mimicking neuroendocrine tumors. Distinguished from biphasic pulmonary blastoma by the absence of primitive malignant mesenchymal stroma.

entities.name: Amphicrine-like carcinoma
entities.anchor: WHO 6th ed. amphicrine-like carcinoma → dual exocrine + neuroendocrine cells, gastric 20q13 gains.
snv: Recurrent — site-specific carcinoma drivers including TP53, APC, KRAS and RB1; rare biallelic MUTYH in syndromic cases
cnv: Characteristic (gastric subset) — recurrent 20q13.12–q13.2 gains (MYT1, NTSR1, ZBTB46), distinct from MiNEN
rearr: Rare reported subset — actionable MAPK fusions (e.g., KANK4::RAF1) in pancreatic acinar-type cases
other: Dual biology — intimately intermixed or single-cell exocrine (mucin/acinar) and neuroendocrine differentiation (≥30% NE morphology + ≥2 NE markers)
entities.pitfall: New entity in WHO Digestive 6th ed. (2026). Distinguished from MiNEN, which shows spatially separate NE and non-NE zones; CD56 alone is insufficient to establish neuroendocrine differentiation.

entities.name: Colorectal low-grade tubuloglandular adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: IBD-associated low-grade tubuloglandular CRC → enriched for IDH1 hotspot mutations.
snv: Characteristic — somatic IDH1 hotspot variants (e.g., R132C), frequently accompanied by KRAS mutations
Cooperating — TP53 and PIK3CA alterations in the colitis-associated precursor pathway
cnv: Associated — colitis-associated chromosomal aneuploidy and arm-level LOH
other: Metabolic/epigenetic — IDH1 mutations drive 2-hydroxyglutarate–mediated hypermethylation; MLH1 loss/MSI-H occurs in a subset
entities.pitfall: New subtype in WHO Digestive 6th ed. (2026) arising almost exclusively in IBD. Bland invasive glands lack stromal desmoplasia, making invasion easy to misread as regenerative crypt distortion or low-grade dysplasia on biopsy.

entities.name: Gastrointestinal NUT-rearranged sarcoma
entities.anchor: GI NUT-rearranged sarcoma → MAD-family (MXD4/MXI1/MGA)::NUTM1 or NUTM2 fusions.
rearr: Defining — NUTM1 or NUTM2 (NUTM2A/G) fusions with MAD-family partners, especially MXD4::NUTM1, MXI1::NUTM1, MXD1::NUTM1 and MGA::NUTM1
other: Distinct from NUT carcinoma — uses MAD-family rather than BET (BRD4/BRD3) partners; BET inhibitors may not be active
entities.pitfall: New entity in WHO Digestive 6th ed. (2026). NUT1 immunohistochemistry is negative in NUTM2-rearranged sarcomas, so RNA sequencing is required when suspected.

entities.name: SWI/SNF complex-deficient undifferentiated carcinoma of the GI tract / pancreas
entities.anchor: SWI/SNF-deficient GI/pancreatic undifferentiated carcinoma → biallelic SMARCA4, SMARCB1, SMARCA2 or ARID1A loss.
snv: Defining mechanism — biallelic inactivation of SMARCA4 (BRG1), SMARCB1 (INI1), SMARCA2 (BRM) or ARID1A
Subset — pancreatic cases stratify into KRAS-mutant vs. KRAS-wild-type/SMARCB1-deficient groups
cnv: Driver — homozygous deletion of SMARCB1 (22q11.2) or SMARCA4 (19p13.2) in subsets
entities.pitfall: Expanded category in WHO Digestive 6th ed. (2026). Pan-cytokeratin is absent or minimal in more than half of cases, closely mimicking sarcoma, melanoma or lymphoma; a SWI/SNF IHC panel is essential.

entities.name: Small-duct intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Small-duct iCCA (WHO 6th ed.) → IDH1/2, BAP1 and FGFR2 fusions.
snv: Driver — IDH1 R132 or IDH2 R172 hotspot variants (enriched in small-duct disease)
Cooperating — BAP1, ARID1A and PBRM1 inactivation
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B deletion
rearr: Driver — FGFR2 fusions (e.g., FGFR2::BICC1 and many partners), strongly enriched in small-duct iCCA
entities.pitfall: Promoted to a standalone entity separate from large-duct iCCA in WHO Digestive 6th ed. (2026). Peripheral mass-forming tumor linked to chronic liver disease/MASLD; actionable IDH1 and FGFR2 alterations are enriched here but not universal.

entities.name: Large-duct intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
entities.anchor: Large-duct iCCA (WHO 6th ed.) → KRAS, TP53, SMAD4 and ERBB2 amplification.
snv: Driver — KRAS activating variants
Cooperating — TP53, SMAD4 and NF1 inactivation
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 amplification (subset)
Cooperating — CDKN2A/B deletion
entities.pitfall: Promoted to a standalone entity separate from small-duct iCCA in WHO Digestive 6th ed. (2026). Perihilar, mucin-producing biology closely overlaps with extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

entities.name: Appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN / HAMN)
entities.anchor: Appendiceal LAMN / HAMN → KRAS + GNAS, with TP53/RNF43 in HAMN.
snv: Driver — high-frequency KRAS and GNAS activating mutations
Progression (HAMN) — TP53 and RNF43 alterations enriched in high-grade lesions
cnv: Associated — low chromosomal instability in LAMN; increased copy-number complexity in HAMN
entities.pitfall: Reclassified under malignant epithelial neoplasms in WHO Digestive 6th ed. (2026) due to risk of pseudomyxoma peritonei. Must be distinguished from benign mucinous adenoma by loss of muscularis mucosae integrity across the entire appendix.

entities.name: Biphasic hyalinizing psammomatous / NF2-inactivated renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: BHP / NF2-inactivated RCC → biallelic NF2 (22q) loss driving Hippo-YAP/TAZ activation.
snv: Defining — biallelic NF2 inactivating variants (nonsense, frameshift, splice-site) lacking VHL, PBRM1, FH or MET drivers
Cooperating — recurrent NSD1, BAP1, APC, SETD2, FAT1 and ARID1B variants
cnv: Driver — 22q deletion involving NF2 (often with CHEK2, SMARCB1, EP300); copy-loss-dominant genome
Cooperating — CDKN2A/CDKN2B deep deletion (subset)
other: Pathway — merlin loss activates Hippo-YAP/TAZ and cell-cycle signaling; aggressive early metastasis with attenuated response to immune checkpoint blockade
entities.pitfall: Emerging malignant RCC entity. Small cells around basement-membrane globules mimic TFEB-rearranged RCC, while high-grade areas mimic papillary RCC or collecting duct carcinoma; merlin IHC loss is a sensitive surrogate.

entities.name: Thyroid-like follicular renal cell carcinoma
entities.anchor: Thyroid-like follicular RCC → EWSR1::PATZ1 fusion, PAX8+/TTF-1−.
rearr: Characteristic — EWSR1::PATZ1 intrachromosomal 22q12.2 rearrangement
entities.pitfall: Listed under other renal tumors in WHO 5th ed.; typically low-grade but capable of distant metastasis and sarcomatoid transformation. Closely mimics metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma; strictly negative for TTF-1 and thyroglobulin.

entities.name: Anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney
entities.anchor: Anaplastic sarcoma of kidney → two DICER1 hits plus TP53 inactivation.
snv: Driver — biallelic DICER1 inactivation (germline or somatic LOF + somatic RNase IIIb hotspot missense)
Cooperating — frequent TP53 inactivating variants; occasional KRAS, NRAS or NF1 alterations
cnv: Cooperating — 17p/TP53 LOH and complex aneuploidy
other: Predisposition — can arise via progression of DICER1-mutant pediatric cystic nephroma; germline DICER1 counseling is indicated
entities.pitfall: Cystic architecture with bizarre pleomorphic spindle cells and heterologous chondroid/rhabdomyoblastic elements mimics anaplastic Wilms tumor, cystic nephroma or rhabdomyosarcoma.

entities.name: Gastric-type endocervical adenocarcinoma
entities.anchor: HPV-independent gastric-type cervical adenocarcinoma → TP53, CDKN2A, STK11 and KRAS.
snv: Driver/cooperating — TP53 (~62%), CDKN2A (~44%), STK11 (~29%, germline in Peutz–Jeghers syndrome) and KRAS (~23%)
cnv: Cooperating — PTEN and CDKN2A deletions; occasional ERBB2 amplification
other: HPV-independent — lacks high-risk HPV; exhibits gastric pyloric mucin (MUC6+) and aggressive peritoneal/ovarian spread
entities.pitfall: Separated here from HPV-associated cervical adenocarcinoma due to distinct HPV-independent genetics. Deceptively bland deep glands cause false-negative Pap smears/biopsies; always exclude metastatic pancreatobiliary/GI adenocarcinoma.

entities.name: Endometrial mucinous carcinoma of gastric type
entities.anchor: Gastric-type endometrial mucinous carcinoma → TP53-mutant yet copy-number-low, with ~30% ERBB2 amplification.
snv: Driver/cooperating — frequent TP53 mutations (40–60%) plus recurrent KRAS/NRAS and PIK3CA variants
cnv: Driver — ERBB2 (HER2) amplification in up to 30% of cases
Characteristic — paradoxically low overall copy-number burden despite TP53 mutation (p53abn/NSMP hybrid)
other: Aggressive ER−/PR− subtype — chemoresistant and distinct from conventional endometrioid mucinous carcinoma
entities.pitfall: Emerging aggressive endometrial entity. Deceptively bland mucinous glands mimic benign mucinous metaplasia, low-grade endometrioid carcinoma, or downward/upward extension from cervical gastric-type adenocarcinoma.

entities.name: STK11 adnexal tumor
entities.anchor: STK11 adnexal tumor → biallelic STK11 (19p13.3) loss; ~50% Peutz–Jeghers syndrome.
snv: Defining — biallelic STK11 (LKB1) inactivating variants (germline in ~50% with Peutz–Jeghers syndrome); lacks FOXL2, DICER1, CTNNB1 and BAP1 drivers
cnv: Driver — 19p13.3 LOH / STK11 loss; recurrent losses of 1p and 11q
other: Pathway — AMPK–mTOR activation; high recurrence and metastasis rates
entities.pitfall: Emerging paratubal malignant neoplasm with polyphenotypic IHC (cytokeratin, inhibin, calretinin, WT1, ER/PR) mimicking FATWO, granulosa cell tumor or mesothelioma; STK11 (LKB1) IHC loss and NGS confirm the diagnosis.

entities.name: NTRK-rearranged spindle cell sarcoma of the uterine cervix / corpus
entities.anchor: Uterine/cervical NTRK sarcoma → NTRK1 or NTRK3 fusion, S100+/CD34+, TRK-inhibitor sensitive.
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B deletion in a subset
rearr: Defining — in-frame NTRK1 or NTRK3 fusions (e.g., TPM3::NTRK1, TPR::NTRK1, EML4::NTRK3, TFG::NTRK3)
entities.pitfall: Entrapped endocervical/endometrial glands create a pseudobiphasic pattern mimicking Müllerian adenosarcoma. Pan-TRK IHC is non-specific (can stain BCOR/YWHAE HG-ESS), so RNA-seq or FISH confirmation is mandatory.

entities.name: COL1A1::PDGFB fusion-associated uterine sarcoma
entities.anchor: COL1A1::PDGFB uterine sarcoma → visceral DFSP counterpart, CD34+, imatinib-responsive.
cnv: Associated — amplification of the COL1A1::PDGFB fusion locus on ring chromosomes or der(22)t(17;22)
rearr: Defining — t(17;22)(q22;q13) COL1A1::PDGFB fusion activating autocrine PDGFRβ signaling
entities.pitfall: Often misclassified as undifferentiated uterine sarcoma or leiomyosarcoma. Diffuse strong CD34 positivity (S100−, desmin−, ER/PR−) in a uterine spindle-cell sarcoma should trigger COL1A1::PDGFB fusion testing.

entities.name: DICER1-associated gynecologic sarcoma
entities.anchor: DICER1 gynecologic sarcoma → two DICER1 hits (LOF + RNase IIIb) ± TP53/RAS.
snv: Defining — biallelic DICER1 mutations (germline/somatic LOF + somatic RNase IIIb hotspot missense)
Cooperating — secondary TP53, NF1 or KRAS/NRAS variants conferring anaplasia and aggressive metastasis
cnv: Cooperating — LOH of wild-type DICER1 allele and variable chromosomal gains/losses
other: Predisposition — flags potential germline DICER1 syndrome; lacks FOXO1 fusions of alveolar RMS
entities.pitfall: Exophytic cervical polypoid masses in adolescents and young adults mimic benign endocervical polyps or Müllerian adenosarcoma; myogenic IHC and DICER1 sequencing prevent misdiagnosis.

entities.name: DEK::AFF2 fusion-associated sinonasal carcinoma
entities.anchor: DEK::AFF2 sinonasal carcinoma → t(6;X) DEK::AFF2 fusion, deceptively bland papillary look.
rearr: Defining — t(6;X) DEK::AFF2 fusion; rare variant AFF2 fusions (e.g., CHD4::AFF2) expand the spectrum
other: Biology — very low TMB, HPV- and EGFR-wild-type, yet high local recurrence, nodal/lung metastasis and frequent PD-L1 expression
entities.pitfall: Emerging subtype of non-keratinizing sinonasal SCC (also skull base/middle ear). Monotonous transitional-like papillary epithelium with neutrophils is repeatedly misdiagnosed as benign inverted papilloma until recurrence or metastasis.

entities.name: Sinonasal teratocarcinosarcoma
entities.anchor: Sinonasal teratocarcinosarcoma → biallelic SMARCA4 loss plus CTNNB1 activation.
snv: Driver — biallelic SMARCA4 (BRG1) inactivating variants (73–82%)
Cooperating — activating CTNNB1 mutations
cnv: Driver — 19p13.2 (SMARCA4) loss/LOH
entities.pitfall: Triphasic sinonasal malignancy (epithelial, mesenchymal and primitive neuroepithelial). Limited biopsies sampling a single component mimic olfactory neuroblastoma, SNUC or SCC; SMARCA4 IHC may show complete or partial loss.

entities.name: Adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma of the head and neck
entities.anchor: Adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma → EWSR1/FUS::FLI1 with diffuse keratin/p40 and distinct methylation.
cnv: Associated — variable copy-number profiles from flat to complex
rearr: Defining — t(11;22) EWSR1::FLI1 fusion (or rare FUS::FLI1)
other: Epigenetic — forms a DNA methylation cluster separate from conventional Ewing sarcoma
entities.pitfall: Diffuse strong cytokeratin and p63/p40 positivity in salivary, sinonasal or thyroid sites mimics basal cell adenocarcinoma, basaloid SCC or NUT carcinoma. EWSR1 FISH alone misses rare FUS::FLI1 cases.

entities.name: Cribriform adenocarcinoma of salivary gland
aliases: cribriform adenocarcinoma of minor salivary gland
entities.anchor: Cribriform salivary adenocarcinoma → PRKD1/2/3 fusions (not PRKD1 E710D SNV).
rearr: Defining — PRKD1, PRKD2 or PRKD3 rearrangements (e.g., ARID1A::PRKD1, DDX3X::PRKD1, ATL2::PRKD3)
entities.pitfall: Distinct fusion-driven counterpart within the polymorphous adenocarcinoma spectrum with higher cervical nodal metastasis (posterior tongue predilection). Optically clear overlapping nuclei mimic metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma (TTF-1−/thyroglobulin−).

entities.name: Skin-analogue primary poroid carcinoma of the head and neck
entities.anchor: Salivary/H&N poroid carcinoma → YAP1::MAML2, YAP1::NUTM1 or WWTR1::NUTM1.
rearr: Defining — YAP1::MAML2, YAP1::NUTM1 or WWTR1::NUTM1 fusions
entities.pitfall: Emerging extracutaneous head-and-neck/salivary entity (2025). NUTM1-fused cases are NUT1 IHC-positive and mimic aggressive NUT carcinoma, while MAML2-fused cases mimic mucoepidermoid carcinoma.

entities.name: CRTC1::TRIM11 cutaneous tumor (malignant/metastasizing subset)
entities.anchor: CRTC1::TRIM11 cutaneous tumor → CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion, SOX10+/TRIM11+, EWSR1-wildtype.
rearr: Defining — CRTC1::TRIM11 gene fusion; lacks EWSR1 rearrangements
other: Behavior — ~12% metastasize to nodes or lungs (sometimes late); immune-cold and refractory to PD-1 inhibitors
entities.pitfall: Added in WHO Skin 5th ed. SOX10 positivity with variable S100/HMB45/Melan-A closely mimics clear cell sarcoma or primary dermal melanoma; EWSR1 FISH negativity plus TRIM11 IHC or RNA-seq resolves it.

entities.name: CNS CIC-rearranged sarcoma
entities.anchor: CNS CIC-rearranged sarcoma → CIC::DUX4 or CNS-enriched CIC::LEUTX.
cnv: Associated — variable aneuploidy; lacks 1p/19q codeletion
rearr: Defining — CIC (19q13) rearrangements, chiefly CIC::DUX4 and CNS-enriched CIC::LEUTX
other: Epigenetic — distinct sarcoma DNA methylation class with poor chemosensitivity
entities.pitfall: WHO CNS5 mesenchymal entity mimicking Ewing sarcoma, embryonal tumor or glioblastoma. CIC break-apart FISH can be falsely negative due to cryptic insertions; RNA-seq or methylation profiling is preferred.

entities.name: Intracranial mesenchymal tumor, FET::CREB fusion-positive
entities.anchor: Intracranial FET::CREB mesenchymal tumor → EWSR1 or FUS fused to CREB1, ATF1 or CREM.
rearr: Defining — EWSR1 or FUS fused to CREB1, ATF1 or CREM (EWSR1::ATF1 linked to worse PFS than EWSR1::CREB1)
other: Epigenetic — distinct DNA methylation profile with significant local recurrence risk
entities.pitfall: Provisional WHO CNS5 entity frequently misdiagnosed as meningioma, solitary fibrous tumor, chordoid glioma or angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma without fusion testing.

entities.name: CNS embryonal tumor with PLAG family gene alteration
entities.anchor: CNS embryonal tumor, PLAG → PLAGL1/PLAGL2 amplification or PLAG1 promoter-hijacking fusion.
cnv: Defining subsets — focal high-level amplification of PLAGL1 (6q24.2) or PLAGL2 (20q11.21, infant-predominant, worse OS)
rearr: Defining subset — PLAG1 (8q12.1) 3' promoter-hijacking fusions (e.g., ASAP1, ADGRG1, TMEM68, TCF4, CHD7::PLAG1)
other: Epigenetic — distinct methylation cluster with imprinted-gene (IGF2, DLK1) and desmin overexpression
entities.pitfall: Emerging pediatric embryonal type with broad histology mimicking ependymoma or embryonal tumor NOS. Must be distinguished from supratentorial ependymoma-like NET_PLAGL1 (EWSR1::PLAGL1).

entities.name: CNS tumor with BCOR/BCORL1 fusion
entities.anchor: CNS BCOR/BCORL1-fused tumor → EP300::BCOR(L1) in older patients, distinct from pediatric BCOR-ITD.
snv: Rare fusion-negative subset — truncating BCOR SNVs/indels matching the same methylation class
cnv: Associated — breakpoints/CNVs at Xp11.4 (BCOR) and 22q12.31 (EP300)
rearr: Defining — EP300::BCOR, EP300::BCORL1, CREBBP::BCORL1, BCOR::CREBBP or MEAF6::CXXC5
other: Epigenetic — distinct methylation class from CNS tumor with BCOR ITD; older median age (~27–30 y)
entities.pitfall: Emerging malignant neuroepithelial type. Oligodendroglioma-like vessels or ependymoma-like pseudorosettes with diffuse OLIG2 positivity frequently lead to misdiagnosis as oligodendroglioma, ependymoma or glioblastoma.

entities.name: High-grade glioma with pleomorphic and pseudopapillary features (HPAP)
entities.anchor: HPAP → IDH/H3-wildtype, TP53/RB1/NF1/NF2 variants + monosomy 13, lacks CDKN2A/B loss.
snv: Recurrent — TP53, RB1, NF1, NF2 (including germline schwannomatosis) and BRAF variants; IDH- and H3-wildtype
cnv: Characteristic — whole-chromosome aneuploidy with monosomy 13 or cnLOH of chr 13, 17 and 22; lacks 9p21 CDKN2A/B deletion
other: Epigenetic — defined by Bethesda CNS methylation classifier; better survival than IDH-wildtype glioblastoma despite high-grade morphology
entities.pitfall: Emerging circumscribed high-grade glioma. Often misdiagnosed as anaplastic ependymoma, astroblastoma, PXA or GBM; juxta-/intraventricular location and diffuse p53 staining are clues.

entities.name: Glioneuronal tumor with ATRX alteration, kinase fusion, and anaplastic features (GTAKA)
entities.anchor: GTAKA → ATRX loss plus recurrent kinase fusion (usually NTRK1/2/3).
snv: Defining — ATRX loss-of-function variants; IDH- and H3-wildtype
rearr: Defining — recurrent kinase fusions, most commonly NTRK1/2/3
other: Epigenetic — distinct methylation class with anaplastic behavior and potential TRK-inhibitor actionability
entities.pitfall: Emerging malignant CNS glioneuronal type. Co-expression of OLIG2 and synaptophysin mimics DGONC, CNS NB-FOXR2 or pediatric HGG; requires RNA fusion panel and methylation profiling.

entities.name: GLI1-altered mesenchymal tumor, malignant/metastasizing
entities.anchor: GLI1-altered mesenchymal tumor → GLI1 fusion or continuous 12q13–15 GLI1/CDK4/MDM2 amplicon.
snv: Progression — secondary TP53 mutations (~20% of GLI1-amplified cases) and CDKN2A loss
cnv: Defining subset (~26%) — continuous 12q13–15 amplification co-amplifying GLI1, CDK4, MDM2, DDIT3, HMGA2 and STAT6 (worse OS than rearranged)
rearr: Defining subset (~74%) — GLI1 fusions, chiefly ACTB::GLI1, MALAT1::GLI1 and PTCH1::GLI1 (rare GLI2 fusions)
entities.pitfall: Added in WHO Soft Tissue & Bone 6th ed. (Oct 2026). Co-amplification of MDM2/CDK4/STAT6 causes misdiagnosis as dedifferentiated liposarcoma or solitary fibrous tumor; nested CD56+ architecture mimics NET or glomus tumor.

entities.name: NFATC2-rearranged sarcoma
entities.anchor: NFATC2-rearranged sarcoma (WHO STB6) → EWSR1::NFATC2 (with fusion amp) or bone-restricted FUS::NFATC2.
cnv: Characteristic — unbalanced amplification of the EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion locus (absent in FUS::NFATC2)
rearr: Defining — EWSR1::NFATC2 (bone/soft tissue; favorable OS) or FUS::NFATC2 (bone; markedly worse prognosis)
entities.pitfall: Split from EWSR1–non-ETS round cell sarcoma in WHO STB6 (Oct 2026). Identical EWSR1/FUS::NFATC2 fusions occur in benign simple bone cysts and vascular malformations (lacking fusion amplification), so morphology/CNV correlation is mandatory.

entities.name: PATZ1-rearranged sarcoma
entities.anchor: PATZ1-rearranged sarcoma (WHO STB6) → EWSR1::PATZ1 via 22q12 inversion/chromothripsis.
cnv: Characteristic — chromosome 22q intrachromosomal inversion / chromothripsis
rearr: Defining — EWSR1::PATZ1 (MN1::PATZ1 is not seen in extra-CNS sarcomas)
other: Epigenetic — polyphenotypic sarcoma clustering separately from low-grade CNS NET-PATZ1 on methylation
entities.pitfall: Split from EWSR1–non-ETS round cell sarcoma in WHO STB6 (Oct 2026). Because EWSR1 and PATZ1 sit ~2 Mb apart on 22q12, standard EWSR1 break-apart FISH is frequently falsely negative; RNA-seq is required.

entities.name: YAP1::KMT2A-rearranged sarcoma
entities.anchor: YAP1::KMT2A sarcoma → YAP1/VIM::KMT2A fusion, MUC4-negative, high lung-metastasis risk.
cnv: Cooperating — frequent CDKN2A homozygous deletion; occasional RB1 loss or MDM2/MDM4 amplification
rearr: Defining — YAP1::KMT2A (often with reciprocal KMT2A::YAP1) or VIM::KMT2A
other: Epigenetic — distinct DNA methylation cluster separate from SEF and LGFMS
entities.pitfall: Emerging sarcoma (soft tissue and bone) with ~50% distant metastasis. Consistently MUC4-negative with deceptive hypocellular fibroma-like zones; KMT2A FISH is often falsely negative and KMT2A is omitted from many solid-tumor panels.

entities.name: MEIS1::NCOA1/2 primitive spindle cell sarcoma
entities.anchor: MEIS1::NCOA1/2 spindle cell sarcoma → visceral/pelvic/GU-GYN whorls, MyoD1/myogenin-negative.
snv: Progression — secondary CTNNB1 hotspot mutations (~14%), linked to recurrence/metastasis
cnv: Associated — occasional 12q13–15 amplifications in high-grade uterine cases
rearr: Defining — MEIS1::NCOA2 or MEIS1::NCOA1 fusion
entities.pitfall: Emerging sarcoma lacking skeletal muscle differentiation (distinguishing it from intraosseous MEIS1::NCOA2 RMS). Nuclear WT1, TLE1 and ER positivity with entrapped tubules mimics monophasic synovial sarcoma or MEST.

entities.name: Kinase-altered spindle cell neoplasm (non-NTRK), malignant
entities.anchor: Non-NTRK kinase-altered spindle cell sarcoma → RAF1, BRAF, RET, ALK, ROS1 or MET fusions.
snv: Alternative subset — activating BRAF point mutations/indels in infantile fibrosarcoma-like cases
cnv: Progression — CDKN2A/B deletion correlates with high-grade malignant transformation
rearr: Defining — fusions involving RAF1 (e.g., PDZRN3, SLMAP, ERC1::RAF1), BRAF, RET, ROS1, ALK, MET or LTK
entities.pitfall: Emerging actionable sarcoma group beyond NTRK. S100/CD34 co-expression (SOX10−) mimics MPNST or solitary fibrous tumor; pan-TRK IHC is negative, requiring broad RNA sequencing.

entities.name: YAP1::TFE3 hemangioendothelioma
entities.anchor: YAP1::TFE3 hemangioendothelioma (WHO STB6) → YAP1::TFE3 fusion, nuclear TFE3+, distinct from EHE.
rearr: Defining — YAP1::TFE3 gene fusion (lacks WWTR1::CAMTA1)
entities.pitfall: Separated from conventional WWTR1::CAMTA1 epithelioid hemangioendothelioma in WHO STB6 (Oct 2026). Displays solid vasoformative epithelioid morphology and diffuse nuclear TFE3; requires fusion confirmation because TFE3 IHC alone is non-specific.

entities.name: Succinate dehydrogenase (SDH)-deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumor
entities.anchor: SDH-deficient GIST (WHO 6th ed.) → SDHA/B/C/D loss or SDHC promoter hypermethylation; KIT/PDGFRA-wildtype.
snv: Defining subset (~50–80%) — loss-of-function (often germline) mutations in SDHA (~30%), SDHB, SDHC or SDHD; KIT/PDGFRA-wildtype
cnv: Cooperating — LOH at the SDHx locus; typically lacks the 14q/22q losses of KIT-mutant GIST
other: Epigenetic subset (~20–50%) — SDHC promoter hypermethylation (Carney triad); succinate accumulation drives genome-wide hypermethylation (including MGMT) and imatinib resistance
entities.pitfall: Separated as a standalone entity in WHO 6th ed. Digestive & STB6 (2026). Still stains for CD117/DOG1; SDHB IHC loss defines the entity, and standard GIST mitotic-size risk models do not reliably predict its indolent yet node-metastasizing course.

entities.name: Epithelioid malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
entities.anchor: Epithelioid MPNST → biallelic SMARCB1 (INI1) loss (~75%), retained H3K27me3, not NF1-driven.
snv: Driver — biallelic SMARCB1 (INI1) inactivation (~75%); generally lacks NF1 and PRC2 (SUZ12/EED) driver profile of conventional MPNST
cnv: Driver — 22q11.23 (SMARCB1) homozygous/hemizygous deletion
other: Distinct biology — retains H3K27me3 and shows diffuse strong S100/SOX10 expression
entities.pitfall: Separated here from conventional MPNST due to distinct SMARCB1-driven genetics. Diffuse S100/SOX10 positivity closely mimics amelanotic melanoma; INI1 loss and absence of melanocytic markers (HMB45/Melan-A) aid distinction.

entities.name: Myeloid neoplasms associated with germline predisposition
entities.anchor: Germline-predisposed myeloid neoplasms → DDX41 (+ somatic 2nd hit), RUNX1, CEBPA, GATA2, ETV6, SAMD9/9L.
snv: Defining germline drivers — without platelet/organ syndrome: DDX41 (up to 4% of adult AML/MDS, usually acquires somatic 2nd-hit DDX41), CEBPA, TP53
Defining germline drivers — with platelet disorder: RUNX1, ANKRD26, ETV6; with organ dysfunction: GATA2, SAMD9, SAMD9L
cnv: Progression — monosomy 7 / del(7q) is a hallmark progression event in GATA2 and SAMD9/SAMD9L syndromes
other: Reversion — somatic copy-neutral LOH can revert pathogenic SAMD9/SAMD9L alleles; germline DDX41 presents late (median ~68 y)
entities.pitfall: WHO-HAEM5 secondary myeloid category. Older age or absent family history does not exclude germline DDX41; always confirm germline status on non-hematopoietic DNA (e.g., skin fibroblasts) before related-donor HSCT.

entities.name: Acute erythroid leukemia
entities.anchor: Acute erythroid leukemia → ≥80% erythroid (≥30% proerythroblasts) + multi-hit TP53 and complex karyotype.
snv: Characteristic — strongly enriched for biallelic/multi-hit TP53 loss-of-function mutations
cnv: Characteristic — complex karyotype (≥3 abnormalities), del(5q), del(7q) and del(17p)/17p cnLOH
entities.pitfall: WHO-HAEM5 entity under AML defined by differentiation (supersedes AML-MR, whereas ICC groups TP53-mutant cases under AML with mutated TP53). Relying solely on p53 IHC can miss truncating TP53 variants.

entities.name: Fibrin-associated large B-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Fibrin-associated LBCL → EBV-driven non-mass-forming aggregates in fibrin/prostheses, lacks MYC/BCL2/BCL6 fusions.
snv: Low burden — sporadic SOCS1, KRAS, KMT2D, CARD11 or IGLL5 variants without a single defining SNV
other: Viral driver — EBV-positive (EBER+) in the vast majority; indolent course often cured by resection alone
entities.pitfall: Separated from DLBCL associated with chronic inflammation in WHO-HAEM5. Confined to fibrin/thrombus in cardiac myxomas, prosthetic valves, grafts or pseudocysts; avoid overtreating as aggressive systemic EBV+ DLBCL.

entities.name: T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: THRLBCL → <10% large B cells, JUNB/DUSP2/SGK1/SOCS1/CREBBP variants + 9p24.1 PD-L1 gain.
snv: Recurrent — JUNB, DUSP2, SGK1, SOCS1 and CREBBP mutations (overlapping with NLPHL)
cnv: Recurrent — 9p24.1 (CD274/PD-L1) gains/amplifications promoting immune evasion
other: Biology — diffuse T-cell/histiocyte-rich background lacking FDC meshworks; forms a biological continuum with Pattern E NLPHL
entities.pitfall: WHO-HAEM5 entity. Needle-core biopsies cannot reliably distinguish THRLBCL from THRLBCL-like NLPHL because any residual nodular/FDC-rich NLPHL area elsewhere in the node establishes NLPHL.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma
aliases: primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphoproliferative disorder
entities.anchor: Primary cutaneous MZL → FAS death-domain mutations (~63%), lacks systemic MALT fusions and MYD88 L265P.
snv: Characteristic — dominant-negative FAS (CD95) death-domain mutations (~63%); recurrent SLAMF1, SPEN and NCOR2; lacks MYD88 L265P
other: Subsets — ~75% class-switched IgG+ (often IgG4+, Th2-rich) and ~25% IgM+; >99% 5-year disease-specific survival
entities.pitfall: Separated from MALT lymphoma in WHO-HAEM5 (termed LPD in ICC 2022). Lacks BIRC3::MALT1/IGH::MALT1 translocations; do not confuse IgG4+ PCMZL with IgG4-related skin disease or overtreat as systemic MALT lymphoma.

entities.name: BCL2-rearrangement-negative, CD23-positive follicle center lymphoma
entities.anchor: BCL2-R− CD23+ follicle center lymphoma → STAT6 + CREBBP mutations, 1p36/TNFRSF14 loss, no t(14;18).
snv: Characteristic — frequent STAT6 (e.g., D419A) and CREBBP co-mutations, plus TNFRSF14 and SOCS1 variants
cnv: Characteristic — 1p36 loss (TNFRSF14), 16p13 loss and 1q gain
other: Biology — lacks IGH::BCL2 t(14;18); predominantly diffuse inguinal/pelvic nodal growth with indolent course; CD23 serves as an IHC surrogate for STAT6 activation
entities.pitfall: ICC 2022 provisional entity (subsumed under WHO-HAEM5 FL with uncommon features). Diffuse CD23+ architecture can be misdiagnosed as CLL/SLL (check CD5−/LEF1− and CD10+/BCL6+) or nodal MZL.

entities.name: Indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract
entities.anchor: Indolent GI NK-cell LPD → JAK3 exon 12 deletions, pSTAT5+, EBER-negative.
snv: Characteristic — activating in-frame deletions in JAK3 exon 12 (canonically p.K563_C565del); occasional BRAF V600E, KRAS or SH2B3 variants
other: Pathway — universal phospho-STAT5 activation, germline TR genes (true NK lineage) and strict EBER negativity
entities.pitfall: New entity in WHO-HAEM5. Must not be misdiagnosed as aggressive ENKTCL or MEITL and overtreated with systemic chemotherapy; EBER negativity, absence of angioinvasion/necrosis and mucosal confinement distinguish it.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS
entities.anchor: Primary cutaneous PTCL, NOS → WHO-HAEM5 aggressive diagnosis of exclusion lacking ALCL fusions.
snv: Heterogeneous — lacks a single entity-defining SNV driver across cases
cnv: Associated — complex, variable copy-number alterations
other: Biology — clonal TR rearrangements, lacks ALK, DUSP22 and TP63 rearrangements; aggressive course (5-year survival ~54%)
entities.pitfall: New standalone entity in WHO-HAEM5. Requires excluding mycosis fungoides, pcALCL, PCGD-TCL, AECTCL and systemic PTCL; aberrant CD20 expression (~18%) can mimic B-cell lymphoma.

entities.name: ALK-positive histiocytosis
entities.anchor: ALK-positive histiocytosis → KIF5B::ALK (or variant ALK fusion), BRAF V600E-negative, ALK-inhibitor responsive.
rearr: Defining — ALK gene fusions in 100%, most commonly KIF5B::ALK (also TPM3, CLTC, EML4, TFG, COL1A2, DCTN1 or TRIM33::ALK)
other: Clinical — spans infantile multisystem, non-infantile multisystem and single-system (often CNS) disease with durable responses to ALK inhibitors
entities.pitfall: New entity in WHO-HAEM5. Unlike LCH and Erdheim–Chester disease, lacks BRAF V600E and canonical MAPK point mutations; ALK IHC and fusion confirmation are essential.

coverage.basis: November 2026 update incorporating WHO 6th edition Digestive System Tumours (July 2026), Breast Tumours (2026), Soft Tissue & Bone Tumours (October 2026), WHO 5th edition Haematolymphoid/Skin/Head & Neck/Urinary/Female Genital/CNS volumes, cIMPACT-NOW Update 8, and peer-reviewed 2024–2026 molecular pathology literature.
merged: Subtypes sharing the same core oncogenic drivers as their parent entity (such as invasive lobular carcinoma with extracellular mucin, colorectal lymphoglandular complex-like adenocarcinoma, pancreatic undifferentiated carcinoma with osteoclast-like giant cells, enteric-type lung adenocarcinoma, and SMARCB1-deficient sinonasal adenocarcinoma) remain nested with updated notes inside their parent entries.
Subtypes and newly recognized WHO 5th/6th-edition or emerging entities with distinct oncogenic drivers are added as standalone entries.
excluded: Benign, preinvasive or predominantly indolent emerging entities (including LOT, EVT, papillary renal neoplasm with reverse polarity, cutaneous cribriform tumor, CNS NET-PATZ1, and VEXAS clonal hemato-inflammatory syndrome).
limitations: Emerging and provisional entities not yet formalized in a WHO Blue Book edition (such as BHP/NF2-inactivated RCC, HPAP, ET-PLAG, CNS BCOR/BCORL1-fused tumor, GTAKA, YAP1::KMT2A sarcoma, MEIS1::NCOA1/2 sarcoma, and skin-analogue head-and-neck poroid carcinoma) are explicitly flagged in their notes.
